audit_notes: Parameters positive and within bounds. Flexural rigidity D = E t^3/(12(1-nu^2)) = 1.5e6*8e-9/(12*0.7599) = 1.32e-3 N m (the candidate's back-of-envelope wrote 1.32 N m, a units slip; its w_max of 1.9 mm is nevertheless correct). Clamped strip: w_max = p a^4/(384 D) = 1.90 mm (0.95 t), peak edge strain 16 t w_max/a^2 = 0.152, identical to the mm-scale parent because p a^2/(E t^2) is unchanged - the extrapolation to cm scale does not raise the strain, it raises the skin thickness (2 mm instead of 0.2 mm), which is what makes the concept more durable. Corrections: at a/t = 10 transverse shear deformation (Mindlin) adds roughly 5-10 % to w, and membrane stretching at w ~ t lowers the edge strain by 15-30 %; the real edge strain is ~0.11-0.13, still above ~0.10. Barnacle release: interfacial shear under a rigid base ~ G*eps ~ 0.5 MPa*0.12 ~ 60 kPa, within the 20-100 kPa range of juvenile barnacle removal stresses on PDMS; adult barnacles on hard spots (>0.1-0.3 MPa) will stay. Load and safety: bladders must be pressure-compensated against ~100 kPa hydrostatic pressure at 10 m draft; while inflated the 2 mm bulges act as large roughness (k+ ~ 400), so pulsing must be restricted to port stays or slow speed. Fatigue: ~1e4 cycles over 5 years at 12-15 % strain is acceptable for filled silicone; the bladder rib bond is the critical detail. The drag benefit (avoided slime and early hard fouling, estimated 15 %) lies outside the solved field; a static coating has zero strain, so there is no meaningful relative baseline in this field: baseline left empty, gain n/a.
